authoredPrompt: This figure is a line drawing of a graphical model laid out as a two-dimensional lattice in oblique projection, built from two kinds of nodes. Open white circles occupy the lattice sites, arranged in three receding rows of three visible sites each; within a row they are joined by horizontal edges that run past the rightmost circle to the frame edge, and between rows by short diagonal edges slanting down and to the left, which likewise continue off the lower-left corner, so the grid reads as a fragment of an unbounded array. A single vertical edge rises from each white circle to a solid gray filled circle, one gray node per site, drawn above and slightly behind its partner. Only the back row carries labels: its white circles are marked with the boldface symbols x_1, x_2, and x_3, and the gray circles directly above them y_1, y_2, and y_3. Because every gray node hangs off exactly one white node while the white nodes alone form the grid, the drawing separates per-site attachments from neighbor-to-neighbor coupling. The structure depicts a Markov random field over a spatial grid, each site carrying a state variable tied to its four lattice neighbors.
authoredInteractions:
- Click any white x node to highlight its four neighboring x nodes and its attached gray y node; all other edges fade, making the local Markov blanket and conditional dependence structure visible.
- Toggle between hidden-state lattice, observation attachments, and full model views; white grid edges, gray vertical links, or both appear in turn, separating neighbor coupling from per-site evidence.
- Slider for coupling strength between neighboring x nodes; neighboring white nodes gradually take on similar shading while y nodes remain fixed, showing how pairwise potentials encourage spatial smoothness across the field.
authoredContext:
To capture relationships over space, a two-dimensional (2D) structure is
useful, called a Markov random field (MRF):

Two-dimensional Markov random field.

An example of how Markov random field models are applied to images is
depicted in the figure, which show a small image region and its context
in the image (the figure [a]). The figure [b] shows an MRF with each
node corresponding to a pixel of the image region. The states of an MRF
can be indicator variables of image segment membership for each pixel.
The states of a hypothetical most-probable configuration of this MRF are
shown as the color of each node in this illustration.

Fig (a) Image to be segmented and a local region of (a) marked in red. (b) Visualization of an MRF of nodes corresponding to image pixels inside the marked region, with states indicating segment membership, for a hypothetical most probable configuration.

discrepancies: Black lattice and observation edges visibly pass through the interiors of the circular nodes, whereas the source nodes occlude the lines and the lines meet the circle boundaries.
The generated lattice is vertically compressed and squat compared with the source; the y-observation links and spacing between oblique rows are too short.
Hidden x nodes have variable light-gray shading from the coupling control, but the source x nodes are uniformly white.
The x and y labels are less faithful in typography and placement; the source uses large serif math-style labels positioned closer to the top-row nodes.
The control panel introduces coupling, view toggles, and Markov-blanket behavior that are not visible concepts in the source figure.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is clearly recognizable as the same MRF lattice, but node-line layering, proportions, default node shading, and extra interactive semantics reduce fidelity.
action_items: Make circular nodes visually occlude edges by rendering opaque fills over rods or by shortening rods so they terminate at circle boundaries.
Increase vertical and oblique-row spacing to better match the taller, more open source lattice.
Keep all hidden x nodes uniformly white in the default view; reserve shading only for an optional interaction state.
Use larger serif/math-style x_i and y_i labels placed closer to the corresponding top-row nodes.
plan_action_items: If the goal is exact textbook fidelity, treat coupling strength and Markov-blanket highlighting as optional explanatory overlays rather than default visual concepts.

feedback.rationale: The figure is faithful and conceptually accurate with consistently high scores, and the remaining issues are minor visual fidelity and optional overlay details unlikely to justify another iteration.
